title: Trump’s Iran Sanctions Have a China Problem
gist: Zongyuan Zoe Liu argues that Trump's 'economic D-Day' financial offensive against Iran depends on China, because Iran's oil trade runs largely through Chinese banks and renminbi-based networks outside dollar-system reach, so the campaign may increase Chinese leverage.

insights.claim: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent declared an 'economic D-Day' against Iran in late August 2026, promising the single greatest financial offensive ever marshaled against an adversary.
insights.speaker: ZONGYUAN ZOE LIU
insights.so_what: Escalating US financial sanctions on Iran are a live risk for oil supply, tanker flows and banks with Iran exposure.

insights.claim: Because Iran's oil trade largely moves through Chinese banks and renminbi-based networks, US sanctions that isolate Iran from the dollar system increasingly depend on financial institutions beyond American control.
insights.speaker: ZONGYUAN ZOE LIU
insights.so_what: Dollar-based sanctions leak through the renminbi channel; Iranian barrels to China may keep flowing, limiting the oil-supply impact of US pressure.

insights.so_what: Watch secondary sanctions on Chinese banks/teapot refiners as the escalation vector in US-China relations and as a test of renminbi payment infrastructure.
